statement: JMOL asks whether, after a party has been fully heard on an issue, a reasonable jury would have a legally sufficient evidentiary basis to find for that party on that issue.
trigger: Party rests; opponent moves for JMOL on a specific element.

statement: On a JMOL motion, stay on trial evidence for the targeted element; do not drift to sympathy, filing conduct, or automatic jury submission.
trigger: Call asks what standard the court should apply to JMOL.

statement: Lost ESI has a sanction ladder: prejudice without intent allows only curative measures no greater than necessary; adverse inference, presumption, dismissal, or default requires intent to deprive.
trigger: lost ESI + prejudice + no deliberate deprivation

statement: Read the choices by sanction severity keyed to mental state: no intent in the stem pushes you away from unfavorable-presumption and case-ending answers.
trigger: one answer cures prejudice; two answers punish as if intent existed

statement: False imprisonment requires intentional confinement. A complaint that pleads only negligent confinement defeats that claim at the motion-to-dismiss stage.
trigger: Complaint labels false imprisonment but says the confinement happened negligently.
authority: Restatement (Second) of Torts §35; Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(b)(6); Ashcroft v. Iqbal.

statement: Amount in controversy is not a likely-verdict test. The pleaded amount controls unless it is legally certain the claim is below the jurisdictional threshold.
trigger: Answer choice talks about unlikely recovery above $75,000.
authority: 28 U.S.C. §1332; St. Paul Mercury Indem. Co. v. Red Cab Co.

statement: On a motion-to-dismiss array, match the reason to the motion. Same outcome plus wrong procedural reason is a trap.
trigger: Two choices talk about amount in controversy while one choice talks about failure to state a claim.

statement: Collateral-order review is narrow. Ordinary discovery orders generally wait for final judgment; expense alone is not effective unreviewability.
trigger: Immediate appeal from a discovery order under the collateral order doctrine.

statement: In an appealability array, sort answers as review-now or review-later. Cut the extreme words first, then ask whether final judgment review is enough.
trigger: Immediate appeal + discovery order + collateral order doctrine.

statement: Attorney-client privilege protects confidential legal-advice communications, not the underlying facts. A fact does not become privileged just because the client told it to a lawyer.
trigger: The discovery request asks for a fact, but the refusal says the fact was told to counsel.
authority: Upjohn Co. v. United States, 449 U.S. 383 (1981); Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(1); Fed. R. Civ. P. 33(a)(2).

statement: Before reading privilege choices, name the object of discovery. If the other side asks for the fact itself, do not let an answer switch you to the lawyer conversation.
trigger: Interrogatory asks for an identity or event fact; objection says the fact was told to counsel.

statement: Rule 54(b) is not automatic. A partial judgment in a multi-claim or multi-party civil action is immediately appealable only if the district court directs entry of judgment and determines that there is no just reason for delay.
trigger: Fewer than all claims or parties resolved; claims remain; order lacks certification language.

statement: When the stem goes out of its way to say the order lacks formal Rule 54(b) language, do not let a partial-dismissal fact do the work by itself.
trigger: One party is out, but other claims remain and formal certification is missing.

statement: For immediate appeal, an order can count as an injunction by practical effect. A command to do or stop doing something may be injunctive even when the caption uses another label.
trigger: Non-injunction caption plus a command to stop conduct until trial.
authority: 28 U.S.C. §1292(a)(1); Carson v. American Brands; Abbott v. Perez.

statement: In a label-vs-function appealability question, read the verb in the order before reading the caption. A stop-command is the navigation signal.
trigger: Order caption says one thing; operative sentence commands a party not to act.

statement: In a diversity case, a defendant's same-transaction counterclaim can use supplemental jurisdiction even below $75,000 unless a specific plaintiff-side §1367(b) bar applies.
trigger: Defendant counterclaim + same incident + no independent amount in controversy.

statement: Read the array as result plus jurisdictional reason. A 'yes' answer is not enough; the reason must be same-event supplemental jurisdiction, not federal question.
trigger: A counterclaim in a diversity case with no independent amount.

statement: When a valid federal statute directly controls a federal-court procedural issue, apply the federal statute before Erie twin-aims balancing.
trigger: Diversity case + state procedural rule + federal statute on point.
authority: 28 U.S.C. § 1391; Hanna v. Plumer; Stewart Organization v. Ricoh.

statement: On a 'which rule controls' call, do not pick the rule that creates the preferred outcome. First identify whether a federal statute directly answers the procedural question.
trigger: Answer choices compare state rule, federal statute, and forum-shopping policy.

statement: For ordinary federal civil actions, venue can sit in the event district or in a defendant-residence district when all defendants reside in that same state; the plaintiff's home is not a venue bucket.
trigger: The call asks which judicial districts are proper and gives accident location plus defendants from different districts of one state.

statement: Read list answers as bucket checklists: keep every valid bucket and reject any answer that adds a false bucket or omits a true one.
trigger: Choices mix event district, defendant districts, and plaintiff home district.

statement: For ordinary diversity jurisdiction, citizenship is measured when the complaint is filed. A later move does not create diversity that was missing at filing.
trigger: A stem gives citizenship at filing and a later domicile change.
authority: 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a); Grupo Dataflux v. Atlas Global Group, L.P.; Mollan v. Torrance

statement: When a jurisdiction stem gives filing-day citizenship and later domicile facts, freeze the snapshot at filing before judging the later facts.
trigger: same-state parties at filing plus a later move before answer or trial

statement: Personal jurisdiction is a waivable Rule 12(b)(2) defense. If it was available and the defendant omitted it from the first answer or first Rule 12 motion, it is waived.
trigger: A defendant answers or files a Rule 12 motion without objecting to personal jurisdiction.

statement: An amended complaint does not automatically revive a Rule 12(b)(2)-(5) defense that was available and waived earlier unless the amendment first creates the defense.
trigger: Plaintiff amends after defendant already failed to raise a known threshold defense.
authority: Gilmore v. Shearson/American Express, Inc.; State Auto Ins. Co. v. Thomas Landscaping & Constr., Inc.; Gnotec Reftele AB order.

statement: Match the jurisdiction word to the call before doing doctrine. Personal jurisdiction is defendant-court power; supplemental jurisdiction is subject-matter power over claims.
trigger: A choice switches from personal jurisdiction to supplemental jurisdiction.

statement: Specific jurisdiction starts with defendant-created forum contacts. Fairness or convenience can defeat jurisdiction after contacts exist, but it cannot create contacts by itself.
trigger: The plaintiff felt harm at home or argues the home forum is fair, while the defendant's conduct all occurred elsewhere.
authority: International Shoe; World-Wide Volkswagen; Walden; Ford.

statement: In a specific-jurisdiction array, sort contacts first and fairness second. A plaintiff-side hardship fact cannot do the work of a defendant-side contact fact.
trigger: Choices mention hardship, injury felt in the forum, and no forum-directed defendant conduct.

statement: Forum property is not a magic key. If the claim is unrelated to the attached property, the forum still needs a defendant-forum-litigation connection.
trigger: A plaintiff attaches a defendant's forum property to sue on an unrelated personal claim.
authority: Shaffer v. Heitner, 433 U.S. 186; International Shoe Co. v. Washington, 326 U.S. 310.

statement: Separate court power from collection. An asset's value may matter after a valid judgment, but it does not answer whether this court can decide the claim.
trigger: An answer asks whether the attached property can satisfy the whole judgment.
